what_happened: The job "Make drain work user-queued (ask --later) requests too" ended failed. The producer's final report was sent back with problems still present. Three acceptance criteria were unmet or not reported: (1) the change must be a channel-set filter in queued_work in steward.rs, with no job-id special case, and a grep of the diff must find none of the named ids in non-test code; (2) the doc comments saying drain takes only the steward channel (steward.rs REQUEST_CHANNEL, drain.rs, docs/decisions.md near line 2206) must be corrected, with a new decision entry and a CHANGELOG line recording the change and why; (3) `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` must all pass. The event lists no blocker or major findings and no failed checks. Nothing was delivered. This is a retry-style rework of the earlier job 20261016-003525-5wwj, which failed on the same goal.
cause: Completion is judged only once, on the producer's final report. Nothing stops the producer from reporting done until it has mapped each criterion to evidence and recorded the gate command results. The failed predecessor job (20261016-003525-5wwj) did not change the process: its unmet criterion, no special-casing of ids, came back in a second job whose request still carried the same structural negative, plus doc and decision-record edits and command runs listed as acceptance items. Nothing carried the earlier gap forward as a checklist. Negative and cross-file criteria (grep of the diff, docs in three places, a decision entry and changelog line) have no mechanical pre-report check, and commands listed as criteria blur who runs them and when. This is the seventh case in this class.
prevention: A completion gate in code that refuses a producer's final report as "done" until it contains a table mapping every acceptance criterion to evidence, and until the gate commands (cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt --check) have actually been run by Athena itself with their results recorded. The gate should also run mechanical checks that can be defined from the criteria: a diff grep for forbidden literals (the named job ids in non-test code) and a check that the named doc files, decisions.md and CHANGELOG are changed. A retry job should inherit the prior failed job's unmet criteria as a required checklist. Gate commands should be moved out of the acceptance list into a standing definition of done.
proposed_request: Make `athena drain` also work user-queued requests (those queued with `ask --later`), not only the steward channel. Outcome: a user-queued request is selected and worked by drain under the same ordering and retry rules as steward-queued items. Requirements: (1) Implement this as a channel-set filter in the shared queue selection function queued_work in steward.rs, so that drain accepts both the steward channel and the user-queued channel. Do not special-case any job id; before reporting, grep the diff and confirm that no job id appears in non-test code. (2) Add a test using ids and items other than the ones from earlier failed jobs, showing that both channels are selected and that ordering and retry are unchanged. (3) Correct every doc comment that says drain takes only the steward channel: REQUEST_CHANNEL in steward.rs, drain.rs, and the passage in docs/decisions.md near line 2206. Add a new decision entry and a CHANGELOG line that record the change and why. (4) Before reporting done, run `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`, and record each command's result in the report. (5) The final report must include a table mapping each numbered requirement above to its evidence (file and line, test name, grep output, command result). Previous attempts (jobs 20261016-003525-5wwj and 20261016-005953-582g) failed because these items were unmet or not reported, so treat this list as a checklist.
